Subject: Intermittent backlog and spikes in generation latency — urgent

Hi Dylan,

Since about 15:30 PT today we've observed repeated bursts where our end-to-end generation p95/p99 jump and a subset of requests hang for >10s. Error rate also climbed briefly to ~2.1%. This is affecting our checkout chat flow (many short, high-QPS calls).

We've attached a trace slice (brightwave_trace_2027-10-11.txt) and a small heap sample. We're on the Redwood Dedicated pool with concurrency cap of 8 per-instance and have not changed our traffic pattern intentionally. Can you triage? This is impacting a live release.

Would like an interim mitigation and an ETA for root cause. We can make time for a quick call.

Thanks,

On Mon, Oct 11, 2027 at 4:12 PM Kayla Rios <kayla.rios@clearport.com> wrote:
> Since about 15:30 PT today we've observed repeated bursts where our end-to-end generation p95/p99 jump and a subset of requests hang for >10s.

I've triaged the trace slice (kv_cache_profile_10-13.json attached) and reproduced locally against a synthetic traffic pattern matching short-prompt, high-QPS calls. Key findings: 

1) KV-cache churn: a large fraction of requests have near-unique prefixes causing heavy KV-cache churn. The cache eviction activity spikes CPU and memory working set, which correlates with increased per-request serialization when the cache manager locks the LRU buckets.

2) Concurrency cap interaction: with the current per-instance concurrency cap (8), backpressure causes head-of-line blocking inside our request queue when several inflight requests trigger heavy cache eviction. That queueing increases observed tail latency even though average utilization is moderate.

3) Amplification path: a small number of long-lived, memory-heavy model runs (batch/embedding background jobs) occasionally collide with short requests, causing the cache manager to rehydrate large segments and prolong lock times.

Short-term repro steps and evidence are in the attached KV profile. This appears to be an architectural interaction between KV-cache eviction locking and hard concurrency limits, not a pure model slowdown.

Suggested immediate mitigations (low-risk order):
- Increase per-instance concurrency cap for ClearPort routes to 12 temporarily (reduces queue head blocking).
- Reduce KV-cache TTLs for short-request routes to avoid large rehydrate operations.
- Apply a patch to stagger cache-eviction critical sections (we have a small diff, runbook_mitigation_patch.diff).

I'll follow up with a PR and test plan. If you want, we can flip the cap change first to see immediate impact while we validate the patch.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
SRE, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: kv_cache_profile_10-13.json, runbook_mitigation_patch.diff)
